$comment: Catalog-level UI builder policy for :remote-catalog, beside its own cover sheet. PER-COMPONENT policy is @BuilderComponent on the sticker, not here. Nothing reads this file yet: it is authored so it can be proved equivalent to the `remote-m3` catalog the preview server synthesises in Kotlin today (ProductionUiBuilderRuntime.remoteM3Catalog), BEFORE the server changes a reader. The contract: https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_CATALOG_CONTRACT.md
$comment_catalogId: Not declared, and that is the point: this module's `system` in catalog.spec.json IS `remote-m3`, which is the id the builder has always authored against. 'A builder catalog is a served catalog' holds here by construction, where the sibling :catalog has to declare it — see that module's policy for why.

wasm.reason: A Remote Compose document is played, not composed. The builder's Wasm canvas has no player, so it draws the widget host frame and placeholders inside it; what the player would draw is a different picture, produced by a different program from the same document.

native.reason: The generated creation-DSL Kotlin compiled against this module's own alpha Remote Compose trio and rasterised by the real player — the same lane that produces every sticker in this catalog.

frame.$comment_adapter: Not a screen. A Remote Compose widget is drawn into a host container of a fixed size, so the frame is the host, not a watch face: `frame/widget-host` rather than the sibling catalog's `frame/round-screen`. This is the second reason `remote-m3` is a catalog of its own rather than a mode of the Wear one.

geometry.$comment: The two host sizes are DECLARED BY THE PREVIEW CONTRACT, not measured after the fact: remote-catalog/src/main/kotlin/ee/schimke/wearm3catalog/remote/WidgetContainerPreviews.kt pins @Preview(widthDp = 216, heightDp = 76) and (216, 124), being 200x60dp and 200x108dp of content plus 8dp of padding on every edge. Every widget sticker in this catalog renders at one of them, so they are the sizes a builder must offer. Recorded here rather than transcribed into the server, which carried both numbers as constants.

colorTokens.$comment: The theme roles a colour property may name. Same Material 3 vocabulary as the sibling :catalog, and stated here for the same reason: a Remote design names roles, and a role the canvas cannot resolve is a literal. Every sticker in this catalog is a RemoteDocument carrying explicit dark-first Material colours, so the values behind these names are the document's rather than a theme's — but the names are what a design writes.

menu.$comment: This catalog's own @CatalogComponent(group = …) vocabulary. Widget Container and Scaffold templates lead because a Remote design starts from a container: everything else goes inside one. Selection buttons, Edge-hugging buttons, Sliders and Steppers are declared only in src/snapshot/kotlin and were missing from this list, so under the snapshot lane the builder appended them after every ordered group and sorted them alphabetically - the order a person saw was not the one stated here.

$comment_builtins: Two, and only because the record cannot carry them. The widget container is the Glance Wear HOST frame — the squircle the launcher draws around a widget, not a `remote-material3` component — so `WidgetContainerPreviews.kt` recreates it through `androidx.glance.wear`'s `WearWidgetPreview` wrapper and there is no component call for a record to find. That is exactly what a builtin is for: "it has no call site, so there is nothing to discover and no sticker to annotate". It matters more than two components' worth: this catalog's own policy says a Remote design starts from a container and everything else goes inside one, and the builder's record-free export routes on the ROOT component id — so a published catalog without these is one whose designs cannot be rooted. They were the blocker in https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/issues/674. `canvas: widget-container` is this catalog CLAIMING an adapter rather than a name anything validates: the Wasm canvas draws both by component id (UiBuilderRenderer's WearWidgetContainerScaffold), and a catalog claiming none would publish "not drawn on the canvas" about something the canvas draws. `remote-m3/lottie` is NOT here though the same argument reaches it — an asset player, no component call. It needs a shelf this catalog does not have (the frozen catalog files it under `Content`, a builder shelf), and inventing one is a catalog decision rather than a transcription. `remote-compose/document` stays out for the older reason: it is a BUILTIN OF THE BUILDER (https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_REMOTE_COMPOSE.md), and declaring it here would be this catalog claiming to own the builder's vocabulary.
$comment_remoteTextVocabulary: WHY remote-m3/remote-text STATES A VOCABULARY AND THE OTHER SEVEN DO NOT. A component that states none is published with the properties DERIVED from its signature, and the derivation keeps only what maps to a JSON scalar: `RemoteText` has twelve parameters and four survive — `text`, `color`, `fontSize`, `maxLines`. `style` is a `RemoteTextStyle` and `textAlign` a `TextAlign`, so both were dropped, and `style` is the parameter this component is actually set through: a design could size text and not scale it. What is stated here is additive — the same four, plus the two the derivation cannot see — and stops there, because a design may only set what the writer writes, and `RemoteContentEmitter` writes these six and the modifier. The four derived names are repeated verbatim rather than left to be merged, because a vocabulary is all-or-nothing per component: state one and it replaces the derivation entirely. ONE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MIGRATION: `style` is undeclared until this lands, so a stored value is tolerated and dropped from validation (https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/pull/840); once it is declared with `allowedValues`, a value outside the eighteen is INVALID rather than undeclared. Material 3 `headlineLarge`, `headlineMedium` and `headlineSmall` have no counterpart in this scale, so a design authored against the borrowed `m3/text` that carries one needs the role mapped by whatever rewrites it onto this component — the `supersedes` migration, not tolerance. Which Wear role each becomes is a design decision for this catalog and is deliberately not guessed here; publishing a `headline` role instead would publish one `RemoteTypography` cannot draw. The set is asserted against the compiled class by RemoteTextStyleVocabularyTest.
$comment_components: Where a component sits on the shelf when the id it derives from does not say. One id per SYMBOL means a component lands on whichever catalog id sorts first: RemoteText is drawn by 29 stickers and arrived under Containment via AppCard, leaving the Text shelf empty. These place the six that were filed somewhere a person would not look, and exclude the one that is not a component.

propertyCapabilities.name: text
propertyCapabilities.notes: The string the component draws. `RemoteText` takes a `RemoteString`, so a design's plain string is written as `"…".rs` and a binding or a state value as the remote expression it names — what the design carries is the same JSON either way.

propertyCapabilities.name: style
propertyCapabilities.notes: A role on this catalog's type scale, written as `style = RemoteMaterialTheme.typography.<role>`. This is the way to set type here: a role carries size, weight, line height and letter spacing together through `RemoteTextStyle`, which is why the catalog's own stickers pass a role OR an explicit size and never both. The eighteen are `RemoteTypography`'s own and are NOT the Material 3 fifteen — there is no `headline` on a watch, and there are five `numeral` roles a time or a metric is set in. A role this class does not have would export as a call that does not compile, so the list is exactly what it publishes.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontSize
propertyCapabilities.notes: Size in sp, as an override on top of `style` rather than a substitute for it — set it alone and everything else about the type comes from the ambient style. Spelled the parameter's own way; a design authored against the borrowed `m3/text` says `fontSizeSp` and the writer reads both. A whole number writes `22.rsp`; a fractional one writes `14.5f.sp.asRemoteTextUnit()`, because `RemoteTextUnitKt` publishes no `Float.rsp`.

propertyCapabilities.name: color
propertyCapabilities.notes: A colour: a `#RRGGBB` literal, which exports as `Color(0x…).rc`, or one of `colorTokens.roles`, which exports as `RemoteMaterialTheme.colorScheme.<role>`.

remote-m3/remote-sticker.excluded: the catalog's own preview frame, not a Remote Compose component: every sticker is drawn inside one and nobody places one in a design.

remote-m3/capturing-wear-widget-preview.excluded: a `private` capture wrapper, not a Remote Compose component: it exists only to hand the widget's encoded document to `IrSidecarChannel` so the render lands a `.rc` sidecar beside the PNG, and it is local at all only until AndroidX's `useSafeFallbackRendererVersion` reaches compose-ai-tools' published wrapper. Same exclusion, and the same reason, as `remote-m3/remote-sticker` above: nobody places a capture frame in a design. It published on the `Widget Container` shelf, beside the two widget-container builtins it wraps.

properties.name: background
properties.notes: The widget's own background, painted by the host as the rounded rect. Defaults to #FF272430, the colour WearWidgetContainer applies to a widget that declares none.

properties.name: horizontalPaddingDp
properties.notes: WearWidgetParams.horizontalPaddingDp; 8 in every shipped preview spec.

properties.name: verticalPaddingDp
properties.notes: WearWidgetParams.verticalPaddingDp; 8 in every shipped preview spec.

properties.name: cornerRadiusDp
properties.notes: WearWidgetParams.cornerRadiusDp: 26 squircle, 999 round, 0 rectangular. The host draws this radius behind the content rather than clipping to it.

$comment_templates: The four template designs this module offers in the New design chooser, as branch-relative paths the design-artifacts pipeline copies from remote-catalog/ui-builder/designs/ onto the delivery branch beside ui-builder.json. Transcribed from the Kotlin builders in compose-ui-builder's UiBuilderTemplates.kt, which remain the live seed until the server reads this entry (SEED_TEMPLATES step 5): the two host frames whose dimensions THIS FILE already declares in frame.geometry.sizesDp, and the two worked designs reproducing android/wear-os-samples' WearWidget sample. Hand-authored designs rather than vendored bytes, so the `groups` exception for :samples-catalog does not apply to them. The chooser's per-template label, supporting text, order and default are NOT expressible in the schema yet (SEED_TEMPLATES step 3, compose-ai-tools): wear-widget-small 'Wear widget · Small (216×76dp)', wear-widget-large 'Wear widget · Large (216×124dp)', hello-widget 'Hello widget' (default), weather-widget 'Weather widget'. Each document's `catalogPin` is the placeholder the server rewrites at creation, never a live revision. The round trip they need — document to generated creation-DSL Kotlin, compiled against this module's own alpha Remote trio — is WidgetTemplateRoundTripTest, the gate only this repository can run. See docs/UI_BUILDER_TEMPLATES.md and https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_SEED_TEMPLATES.md
$comment_code: No `code` block yet, so the export stays `record`. A Remote widget is written in the creation DSL rather than in Compose, which is a `code.language` and a set of structural templates — and both arrive with the template engine, not ahead of it. Until then the export prints call sites from the record, which is what it already does.
